nodes.label: M12 base case: 80k cumulative signups, 50% global-weighted, 6% conversion, $28/mo ARPU → ~2,400 payers ≈ $806k B2C ARR
nodes.rationale: Conversion applies only to the global-weighted free base, never total signups — the explicit fix to the 'blended ARPU is fiction' trap; India revenue is off the ARPU line entirely.

nodes.label: One-broker B2B line: ₹20/active-MAU/mo, 300k MAU ≈ $867k full-ramp ARR; $1M combined by M12 only if pilot books ~$0.5M
nodes.rationale: Exactly one broker (Sensibull→Zerodha blueprint) — stacking B2B logos on the same SEBI-compliance demand is cannibalistic; the logo de-risks the exit more than it adds revenue, and it is a hard, key-man, ~9-month enterprise sale.

nodes.label: Acquisition (~M18-30, $2.5-3.5M combined ARR, 8-12x → $24-36M) as the likelier millions outcome; $10-20M tuck-in floor
nodes.rationale: For a 3-person capital-light India-based team, an acquisition by an Indian broker, global neobroker, charting platform or EdTech/AI buyer is more probable than grinding B2C to $10M ARR; revenue is the credibility engine, architecture and dataset earn the exit.

nodes.label: Behavioral dataset of decision traces (cone-drags, Greek tweaks, paper trades, confusion points) as the core hard-to-clone acquirer asset
nodes.rationale: No GPT wrapper, OptionStrat, or TradingView owns decision traces — they own dashboards; the dataset plus an AI fine-tuned on confusion-resolution is what a buyer is actually buying.
